title.zh: 卷八十三 列傳第三十三: 郭孝恪 張儉 蘇定方 薛仁貴 程務挺 張士貴 趙道興
title.en: Volume 83 Biographies 33: Guo Xiaoke, Zhang Jian, Su Dingfang, Xue Rengui, Cheng Wuting, Zhang Shigui, Zhao Daoxing
title.raw: 卷八十三 列傳第三十三: 郭孝恪 張儉 蘇定方 薛仁貴 程務挺 張士貴 趙道興 Volume 83 Biographies 33: Guo Xiaoke, Zhang Jian, Su Dingfang, Xue Rengui, Cheng Wuting, Zhang Shigui, Zhao Daoxing

sentences.zh: 郭孝恪張儉蘇定方薛仁貴程務挺張士貴趙道興

translations.literal: Guo Xiaoke, Zhang Jian, Su Dingfang, Xue Rengui, Cheng Wuting, Zhang Shigui, Zhao Daoxing
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoke, Zhang Jian, Su Dingfang, Xue Rengui, Cheng Wuting, Zhang Shigui, and Zhao Daoxing

sentences.zh: 郭孝恪，許州陽翟人也，少有誌節。

translations.literal: Guo Xiaoke was a man of Yangzhai in Xu Prefecture. From youth he had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoke was a native of Yangzhai in Xu Prefecture. Even as a young man he showed firm purpose and moral backbone.

sentences.zh: 隋末，率鄉曲數百人附於李密，密大悅之，謂曰：“昔稱汝潁多奇士，故非謬也。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui he led several hundred fellow townsmen to attach to Li Mi. Mi was greatly pleased with him and said, "It was once said that Runan and Yingchuan produce many extraordinary men — that was no empty saying."
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui dynasty was collapsing, he led several hundred neighbors to join Li Mi. Mi was delighted and told him, "People used to say Runan and Yingchuan breed remarkable men — they were not wrong."

sentences.zh: ”令與徐勣守黎陽。

translations.literal: " He ordered him together with Xu Ji to guard Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then assigned him, together with Xu Shiji, to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 後密敗，勣令孝恪入朝送款，封陽翟郡公，拜宋州刺史。

translations.literal: Later when Mi was defeated, Ji ordered Xiaoke to enter court and offer allegiance. He was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangzhai commandery and appointed prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat, Shiji sent Xiaoke to the Tang court to submit. He was created Duke of Yangzhai and made prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 令與徐勣經營武牢已東，所得州縣，委以選補。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Xu Ji to administer east of Wulao Pass; for all prefectures and counties obtained, they were entrusted with selection and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu Shiji were charged with governing everything east of Wulao Pass, with authority to appoint officials in the prefectures and counties they took.

sentences.zh: 其後，竇建德率眾來援王世充，孝恪於青城宮進策於太宗曰：“世充日踧月迫，力盡計窮，懸首麵縛，翹足可待。

translations.literal: Subsequently Dou Jiande led his masses to aid Wang Shichong. At Qingcheng Palace Xiaoke advanced a stratagem to Emperor Taizong, saying: "Shichong day by day is pressed and month by month driven; strength exhausted and schemes spent — to hang his head and bind his face, one need only lift a foot and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Dou Jiande marched to relieve Wang Shichong, Xiaoke presented a plan to Emperor Taizong at Qingcheng Palace: "Shichong grows more desperate every day; his strength and stratagems are spent. He is ready to surrender at a word — we need only wait."

sentences.zh: 建德遠來助虐，糧運阻絕，此是天喪之時。

translations.literal: Jiande comes from afar to aid tyranny; grain transport is cut off — this is Heaven's time of destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande has come a long way to support a tyrant, and his supply lines are already broken. Heaven itself is turning against him.

sentences.zh: 請固武牢，屯軍汜水，隨機應變，則易為克殄。

translations.literal: I beg to secure Wulao, station troops at Sishui, and adapt as circumstances require — then he can easily be annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold Wulao firm, camp at Sishui, and respond flexibly as events unfold, both enemies can be destroyed with ease.

sentences.zh: ”太宗然其計。

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizong approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 及破建德，平世充，太宗於洛陽置酒高會諸將曰：“郭孝恪謀擒建德之策，王長先龍門下米之功，皆出諸人之右也。

translations.literal: When Jiande was broken and Shichong pacified, Taizong at Luoyang set out wine for a grand gathering of the generals and said: "Guo Xiaoke's plan to capture Jiande, and Wang Changxian's achievement of grain below Longmen — both surpass the rest of the men."
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande was defeated and Shichong subdued, Taizong held a grand banquet for his generals in Luoyang and declared, "Guo Xiaoke's scheme to take Jiande and Wang Changxian's feat of securing grain below Longmen both outshine everyone else's contributions."

sentences.zh: ”曆遷貝、趙、江、涇四州刺史，所在有能名。

translations.literal: " He successively transferred through the four prefectures of Bei, Zhao, Jiang, and Jing as prefect; everywhere he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on to serve as prefect of Bei, Zhao, Jiang, and Jing in turn, earning a name for competence wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 入為太府少卿，轉左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then was transferred to General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice minister of the imperial treasury, then promoted to general of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年，累授金紫光祿大夫，行安西都護、西州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan he was cumulatively appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Protector-General of Anxi and prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 642 he was given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and appointed acting Protector-General of Anxi and prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 其地高昌舊都，士流與流配及鎮兵雜處，又限以沙磧，與中國隔絕。

translations.literal: The place was the old capital of Gaochang; gentry, exiles, and garrison troops were mixed together, and moreover it was bounded by sandy desert, cut off from central China.
translations.idiomatic: The region was the former capital of Gaochang, where educated exiles, banished convicts, and frontier garrisons lived side by side, separated from the heartland by vast deserts.

sentences.zh: 孝恪推誠撫禦，大獲其歡心。

translations.literal: Xiaoke extended sincerity to comfort and govern them, and greatly won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke governed them with open sincerity and won their deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 初，王師之滅高昌也，製以高昌所虜焉耆生口七百盡還之。

translations.literal: At first, when the royal army destroyed Gaochang, an order was issued that the seven hundred Yanqi captives taken by Gaochang be entirely returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army had earlier destroyed Gaochang, an edict ordered that all seven hundred Yanqi people whom Gaochang had seized be sent home.

sentences.zh: 焉耆王尋叛歸欲穀可汗，朝貢稀至。

translations.literal: The king of Yanqi soon rebelled and went over to the Yabgu Qaghan; tribute missions became rare.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yanqi soon rebelled and submitted to the Western Turks; tribute from Yanqi all but ceased.

sentences.zh: 令孝恪伺其機便，因表請擊之。

translations.literal: Xiaoke was ordered to watch for an opportune moment and accordingly memorialized requesting an attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court told Xiaoke to watch for an opening and he memorialized asking permission to strike.

sentences.zh: 以孝恪為安西道行軍總管，率步騎三千出銀山道以伐焉耆。

translations.literal: Xiaoke was made Commander-in-Chief of the Anxi campaign army, leading three thousand infantry and cavalry by the Yinshan road to attack Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke was appointed commander of the Anxi campaign force and led three thousand foot and horse soldiers along the Yinshan route against Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 孝恪夜襲其城，虜其王龍突騎支。

translations.literal: Xiaoke raided the city by night and captured its king Long Tuqizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke stormed the city at night and took its king, Long Tuqizhi, prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，璽書勞之曰：“卿破焉耆，虜其偽王，功立威行，深副所委。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and sent an imperial edict of commendation, saying: "You broke Yanqi and captured its false king; merit established and authority displayed — deeply answering what was entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was overjoyed and sent a sealed letter of praise: "You have crushed Yanqi and taken its pretender king. Your achievements match the trust I placed in you."

sentences.zh: 但焉耆絕域，地阻天山，恃遠憑深，敢懷叛逆。

translations.literal: But Yanqi is a remote region; the land is blocked by the Heavenly Mountains. Relying on distance and depth, it dared harbour rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi lies at the edge of the empire, shielded by the Tianshan range. Trusting in its remoteness, it dared to rebel.

sentences.zh: 卿望崇位重，報效情深，遠涉沙場，龔行罰罪。

translations.literal: Your repute is lofty and your post weighty; your devotion to repayment runs deep. You crossed the distant desert campaign and marched to execute punishment.
translations.idiomatic: You bear heavy rank and high reputation, and your loyalty runs deep. You crossed the battlefields of the west to carry out imperial punishment.

sentences.zh: 取其堅壁，曾不崇朝；

translations.literal: You took their strong walls in less than a morning;
translations.idiomatic: You seized their fortified walls in less than a single morning;

sentences.zh: 再廓遊魂，遂無遺寇。

translations.literal: you cleared the wandering spirits again, and no rebel band remained.
translations.idiomatic: you swept away the scattered enemy so that not a single bandit was left.

sentences.zh: 緬思竭力，必大艱辛。

translations.literal: Reflecting on your exerting every effort, it must have been greatly arduous.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of the effort you must have expended, I know the hardship was immense.

sentences.zh: 超險成功，深足嘉尚。

translations.literal: Success beyond peril is deeply worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: To succeed across such dangers is truly admirable.

sentences.zh: ”俄又以孝恪為昆丘道副大總管以討龜茲，破其都城。

translations.literal: " Soon after, Xiaoke was again made deputy supreme commander of the Kunqiu campaign to attack Kucha and broke its capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward Xiaoke was made deputy supreme commander of the Kunqiu campaign against Kucha and captured its capital.

sentences.zh: 孝恪自留守之，餘軍分道別進，龜茲國相那利率眾遁逃。

translations.literal: Xiaoke himself remained to garrison it; the rest of the army advanced by separate routes. The Kucha chancellor Nali led his forces in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke stayed behind to hold the city while the other columns pressed on. The Kucha chancellor Nali fled with his followers.

sentences.zh: 孝恪以城外未賓，乃出營於外，有龜茲人來謂孝恪曰：“那利為相，人心素歸，今亡在野，必思為變。

translations.literal: As those outside the city had not yet submitted, Xiaoke moved camp outside. A man of Kucha came and said to Xiaoke: "Nali as chancellor has long held men's hearts; now he is at large in the wilds and is sure to think of making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Because the countryside had not yet submitted, Xiaoke moved his camp outside the walls. A Kuchean came to warn him: "Nali has long been the people's choice as minister. Now that he is at large in the hills, he is sure to plot an uprising.

sentences.zh: 城中之人，頗有異志，公宜備之。

translations.literal: Many in the city harbour contrary intentions — you ought to guard against them."
translations.idiomatic: Many inside the city are of doubtful loyalty. You should take precautions."

sentences.zh: ”孝恪不以為虞。

translations.literal: " Xiaoke did not regard it with concern.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaoke paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 那利等果率眾萬餘，陰與城內降胡表裏為應。

translations.literal: Nali and others indeed led more than ten thousand men, secretly coordinating with surrendered Hu inside the city in inner-outer response.
translations.idiomatic: Nali did in fact rally more than ten thousand men and secretly coordinated with Turkic collaborators inside the city.

sentences.zh: 孝恪失於警候，賊將入城鼓噪，孝恪始覺之，乃率部下千餘人入城，與賊合戰。

translations.literal: Xiaoke failed in watch and guard; the bandits were about to enter the city with drum and clamour when Xiaoke first became aware. He then led more than a thousand subordinates into the city and joined battle with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke had been careless with his sentries. The rebels were already storming the gates with drums and shouts before he realized what was happening. He rushed into the city at the head of a thousand men and fought hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 城中人復應那利，攻孝恪。

translations.literal: People in the city again responded to Nali and attacked Xiaoke.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople rose for Nali and turned on Xiaoke.

sentences.zh: 孝恪力戰而入，至其王所居，旋復出，戰於城門，中流矢而死，孝恪子待詔亦同死於陣。

translations.literal: Xiaoke fought his way in with force, reaching the king's residence, then turned and came out again, fighting at the city gate; he was struck by a stray arrow and died. Xiaoke's son Daizhao also died together in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke fought his way to the royal quarters, then fought his way out again at the gate, where a stray arrow killed him. His son Daizhao fell beside him in the melee.

sentences.zh: 賊竟退走，將軍曹繼叔復拔其城。

translations.literal: The bandits in the end retreated and fled; General Cao Jishu again recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels eventually fled, and General Cao Jishu recaptured the city.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，初責孝恪不加警備，以致顛覆；

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it, at first he blamed Xiaoke for not adding vigilance and guard, causing overturn;
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard the news, he first blamed Xiaoke for failing to take precautions, which had led to disaster;

sentences.zh: 後又憐之，為其家舉哀。

translations.literal: later he again pitied him and held mourning for his family.
translations.idiomatic: but later he took pity on him and ordered mourning for the family.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追贈安西都護、陽翟郡公，待詔贈遊擊將軍，仍賻物三百段。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Protector-General of Anxi and Duke of Yangzhai commandery; Daizhao was posthumously given General of Guerrilla Warfare, and three hundred lengths of goods were still bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's accession, Xiaoke was posthumously made Protector-General of Anxi and Duke of Yangzhai; Daizhao was posthumously made general of guerrilla warfare, and the family received three hundred rolls of goods as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 孝恪性奢侈，仆妾器玩，務極鮮華，雖在軍中，床帳完具。

translations.literal: Xiaoke by nature was extravagant; servants, concubines, vessels, and curios — all were pursued to utmost splendour and brilliance. Even in the army, bed and canopy were complete and equipped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke was by nature extravagant: his servants, concubines, and furnishings were always as lavish as possible, and even on campaign his camp was fully appointed with bedding and hangings.

sentences.zh: 嚐以遺行軍大總管阿史那社爾，社爾一無所受。

translations.literal: He once sent gifts to the campaign supreme commander Ashina She'er; She'er accepted not a single item.
translations.idiomatic: He once tried to send gifts to the supreme commander Ashina She'er, who refused every one.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之曰：“三將優劣之不同也。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he said: "The three generals differ in excellence and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong remarked when he heard of this, "Here you see how three commanders differ in character.

sentences.zh: 郭孝恪今為寇虜所屠，可謂自貽伊咎耳。

translations.literal: Guo Xiaoke now is slaughtered by bandit foes — it may be said he brought calamity on himself."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoke has now been cut down by the enemy — he brought it on himself."

sentences.zh: ”次子待封，高宗時，官至左豹韜衛將軍。

translations.literal: " The second son Daifeng, in Gaozong's time, reached office as General of the Left Leopard Bow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " His second son Daifeng rose under Gaozong to general of the Left Leopard Bow Guard.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，與薛仁貴率兵討吐蕃，於大非川戰敗，減死除名。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era, together with Xue Rengui he led troops to attack the Tibetans; at the battle of Dafei River they were defeated, and his death penalty was reduced but his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng period he joined Xue Rengui in a campaign against Tibet, was defeated at Dafeichuan, and was spared execution only to be stripped of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 少子待聘，長安中官至宋州刺史。

translations.literal: The youngest son Daipin, in the Chang'an era, reached office as prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Daipin later served as prefect of Songzhou in the Chang'an period.

sentences.zh: 張儉，雍州新豐人，隋相州刺史、皖城公威之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian was a man of Xinfeng in Yong Prefecture, grandson of the Sui prefect of Xiangzhou and Duke of Wancheng, Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian came from Xinfeng in Yong Prefecture and was the grandson of Zhang Wei, the Sui prefect of Xiangzhou who had been enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 父植，車騎將軍、連城縣公。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Liancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had been general of chariots and cavalry and Duke of Liancheng.

sentences.zh: 儉即高祖之從甥也。

translations.literal: Jian was Gaozu's maternal nephew's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu on the maternal side.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，以軍功累遷朔州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, through military achievement he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was promoted on merit to prefect of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 時頡利可汗自恃強盛，每有所求，輒遣書稱敕。

translations.literal: At the time the Qaghan Jieli relied on his strength and prosperity; whenever he had a request he would send a letter styled as an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Qaghan Jieli, confident in his power, would send demands couched as if they were imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 緣邊諸州，遞相承稟。

translations.literal: The border prefectures one after another received and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures had been complying one after another.

sentences.zh: 及儉至，遂拒不受，太宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: When Jian arrived, he then refused and did not accept; Taizong heard and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian took office he refused outright. Taizong heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 儉又廣營屯田，歲致穀十萬斛，邊糧益饒。

translations.literal: Jian also broadly established military colonies; each year he delivered one hundred thousand bushels of grain, and border provisions grew more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also expanded military farming colonies, delivering a hundred thousand bushels of grain a year until frontier stores were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 及遭霜旱，勸百姓相贍，遂免饑餒，州境獨安。

translations.literal: When frost and drought struck, he urged the common people to support one another, and thus hunger was avoided; within the prefecture alone there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: When frost and drought struck, he urged the people to help one another, so that famine was averted and his prefecture alone remained calm.

sentences.zh: 後檢校勝州都督，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he was made acting military governor of Shengzhou and left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made acting governor of Shengzhou but resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 儉前在朔州，屬李靖平突厥之後，有思結部落，貧窮離散，儉招慰安集之。

translations.literal: When Jian was earlier at Shuozhou, after Li Jing pacified the Turks there was the Sijie tribe, poor and scattered; Jian recruited and comforted them to gather and settle.
translations.idiomatic: While he was at Shuozhou, after Li Jing's defeat of the Turks, the impoverished and scattered Sijie tribe came under his care; he gathered and settled them through gentle persuasion.

sentences.zh: 其不來者，或居磧北，既親屬分住，私相往還，儉並不拘責，但存綱紀，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Those who did not come, some dwelt north of the desert; as kin were distributed in residence, they privately went back and forth — Jian altogether did not restrain and blame them, but only preserved discipline and regulation, keeping them on loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stayed away, some living north of the desert, continued to visit relatives across the border. Jian did not punish them; he merely upheld basic order and kept them loosely tied to the empire.

sentences.zh: 及儉移任，州司謂其將叛，遽以奏聞。

translations.literal: When Jian was transferred, the prefectural office said they were about to rebel and hurriedly reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian was transferred, local officials assumed the tribe was about to rebel and rushed a report to the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議發兵進討，仍起儉為使，就觀動靜。

translations.literal: The court deliberated sending troops to advance and attack; they still raised Jian as envoy to go observe movements and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated sending troops, but instead recalled Jian as envoy to investigate the situation on the spot.

sentences.zh: 儉單馬推誠，入其部落，召諸首領，布以腹心，鹹匍匐啟顙而至，便移就代州。

translations.literal: Jian alone on horseback extended sincerity, entered their tribe, summoned all the chieftains, and laid open his inner heart; all crawled prostrate with foreheads to the ground and came, and he then moved them to settle at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Riding alone, Jian entered their camps in good faith, summoned the chiefs, and spoke frankly to them. They came forward prostrate, and he relocated them to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 即令檢校代州都督。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered acting military governor of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly made acting governor of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 儉遂勸其營田，每年豐熟。

translations.literal: Jian then urged them to establish military colonies; every year there was rich harvest.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded them to farm military colonies, and harvests were abundant year after year.

sentences.zh: 慮其私蓄富實，易生驕侈，表請和糴，擬充貯備，蕃人喜悅。

translations.literal: Fearing their private stores would grow rich and solid and easily breed arrogance and extravagance, he memorialized requesting government purchase at fair price, intending to fill storage reserves; the foreigners were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that private wealth would breed arrogance, he petitioned for government grain purchases to fill the frontier granaries. The tribesmen were delighted.

sentences.zh: 邊軍大收其利。

translations.literal: The border army greatly reaped this benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier armies profited greatly.

sentences.zh: 遷營州都督，兼護東夷校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Yingzhou, concurrently Protector of the Eastern Yi Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Yingzhou and made protector of the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 太宗將征遼東，遣儉率蕃兵先行抄掠。

translations.literal: Taizong was about to campaign against Liaodong and dispatched Jian to lead foreign troops ahead in raiding.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to campaign against Liaodong, he sent Jian ahead with tribal auxiliaries to harry the enemy.

sentences.zh: 儉軍至遼西，為遼水汛漲，久而未渡，太宗以為畏懦，召還。

translations.literal: Jian's army reached Liaoxi; because the Liao River was in flood swell, for a long time they did not cross. Taizong thought it cowardice and recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian reached Liaoxi but could not cross the flooded Liao River for a long time. Taizong took this for timidity and ordered him back.

sentences.zh: 儉詣洛陽謁見，麵陳利害，因說水草好惡，山川險易，太宗甚悅，仍拜行軍總管，兼領諸蕃騎卒，為六軍前鋒。

translations.literal: Jian went to Luoyang to have audience, face to face stating advantage and harm, and thereby spoke of water and grass good and bad, mountains and rivers perilous and easy. Taizong was greatly pleased and still appointed him campaign commander-in-chief, concurrently leading all foreign cavalry soldiers as vanguard of the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jian went to Luoyang, explained the strategic situation in person, and described pasture, terrain, and routes in detail. Taizong was delighted, reappointed him campaign commander, put him at the head of the tribal cavalry, and made him vanguard of the six armies.

sentences.zh: 時有獲高麗候者，稱莫離支將至遼東，詔儉率兵自新城路邀擊之，莫離支竟不敢出。

translations.literal: At the time there was a captured Goguryeo scout who said Molizhi was about to reach Liaodong. An edict ordered Jian to lead troops by the Xincheng route to intercept him; Molizhi in the end did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: A captured Goguryeo scout reported that Molizhi was marching on Liaodong. Jian was ordered to ambush him on the Xincheng road, and Molizhi never dared advance.

sentences.zh: 儉因進兵渡遼，趨建安城，賊徒大潰，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Jian thereby advanced troops across the Liao, pressing toward Jian'an city; the rebel bands greatly collapsed, and several thousand heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then crossed the Liao, drove on Jian'an, routed the enemy, and took several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 以功累封皖城郡公，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Through achievement he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng commandery; rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: For his merits he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 其後，改東夷校尉為東夷都護，仍以儉為之。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Eastern Yi Colonel was changed to Eastern Yi Protector-General, and Jian was still made to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the office of Eastern Yi colonel was elevated to Eastern Yi protector-general, and Jian retained the post.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui era he was given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於官，年六十，諡曰密。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office at age sixty; his posthumous title was Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yonghui he died in office at the age of sixty. His posthumous name was Mi.

sentences.zh: 儉兄大師，累以軍功仕至太仆卿、華州刺史、武功縣男。

translations.literal: Jian's elder brother Dash, through repeated military achievement, served up to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, prefect of Huazhou, and Baron of Wugong county.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's elder brother Dash rose through military service to minister of the imperial stud, prefect of Huazhou, and Baron of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 儉弟延師，永徽初，累授左衛大將軍，封范陽郡公。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Yanshi, at the beginning of Yonghui, was repeatedly appointed Grand General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanshi was made grand general of the Left Guard early in Yonghui and enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 延師廉謹周慎，典羽林屯兵前後三十餘年，未嚐有過，朝廷以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yanshi was frugal, careful, thorough, and cautious; he directed the Feathered Forest garrison troops for more than thirty years before and after, and never once had a fault — the court for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi was frugal, careful, and conscientious. He commanded the Feathered Forest garrison for more than thirty years without a single blemish on his record, for which the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，卒官，贈荊州都督，諡曰敬，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo he died in office; he was posthumously given military governor of Jingzhou, posthumous title Jing, and buried accompanying Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 663, was posthumously made governor of Jingzhou with the posthumous name Jing, and was buried near Taizong's Zhaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 唐製三品已上，門列棨戟，儉兄弟三院，門皆立戟，時人榮之，號為“三戟張家”。

translations.literal: Tang regulations: from third rank upward, halberds were arrayed at the gate. The three compounds of the Jian brothers all had halberds standing at their gates; men of the time honoured them and called them "the Zhang family of three halberds."
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang custom, officials of third rank and above displayed ceremonial halberds at their gates. All three Zhang brothers' households bore them, and contemporaries honoured them as "the Zhang family of three halberds."

sentences.zh: 蘇定方，冀州武邑人也。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang was a man of Wuyi in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang was a native of Wuyi in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父邕，大業末，率鄉閭數千人為本郡討賊。

translations.literal: His father Yong, at the end of the Daye era, led several thousand fellow villagers and townsmen of the commandery to suppress bandits for the native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong, at the end of the Sui, led several thousand local men in suppressing bandits on behalf of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 定方驍悍多力，膽氣絕倫，年十餘歲，隨父討捕，先登陷陣。

translations.literal: Dingfang was fierce and brave with great strength; courage and spirit were unmatched. At more than ten years of age he followed his father in pursuit and capture, first ascending and breaking formations.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang was ferociously strong and utterly fearless. Before he was fifteen he rode with his father on punitive expeditions, always first over the wall and into the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 父卒，郡守又令定方領兵，破賊首張金稱於郡南，手斬金稱，又破楊公卿於郡西，追奔二十餘里，殺獲甚眾，鄉黨賴之。

translations.literal: When his father died, the commandery governor again ordered Dingfang to lead troops. He broke the bandit chief Zhang Jincheng south of the commandery and personally beheaded Jincheng; he again broke Yang Gongqing west of the commandery, pursued in flight more than twenty li, and killed and captured in great numbers — the village and district relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death the prefect put Dingfang in command. He defeated the rebel Zhang Jincheng south of the prefecture and killed him with his own hand, then routed Yang Gongqing to the west, pursued the fugitives for more than twenty li, and killed or captured a great host. The region owed its safety to him.

sentences.zh: 後仕竇建德，建德將高雅賢甚愛之，養以為子。

translations.literal: Later he served Dou Jiande; Jiande's general Gao Yaxian greatly loved him and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the service of Dou Jiande, whose general Gao Yaxian took a liking to him and adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 雅賢俄又為劉黑闥攻陷城邑，定方每有戰功。

translations.literal: Yaxian soon again for Liu Heidan attacked and took cities and towns; Dingfang every time had military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaxian campaigned with Liu Heidan in seizing towns, Dingfang distinguished himself in every battle.

sentences.zh: 及黑闥、雅賢死，定方歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Heidan and Yaxian died, Dingfang returned to his village and district.
translations.idiomatic: After Heidan and Yaxian were killed, Dingfang went home.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為匡道府折衝，隨李靖襲突厥頡利於磧口。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was Colonel Who Breaks the Ranks of Kuangdao prefecture, following Li Jing in the surprise attack on the Turk Jieli at Qikou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became a frontier colonel of Kuangdao and joined Li Jing's surprise attack on the Turk qaghan Jieli at Qikou.

sentences.zh: 靖使定方率二百騎為前鋒，乘霧而行，去賊一里許，忽然霧歇，望見其牙帳，馳掩殺數十百人。

translations.literal: Jing ordered Dingfang to lead two hundred cavalry as vanguard, riding through fog; when about one li from the foe the fog suddenly lifted — they saw the royal tent and galloped to cover and kill several tens and hundreds of men.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Dingfang ahead with two hundred horsemen. They rode through fog until, a li from the enemy camp, the mist lifted and revealed the royal tent. They charged and killed scores of men.

sentences.zh: 頡利及隋公主狼狽散走，餘眾俯伏，靖軍既至，遂悉降之。

translations.literal: Jieli and the Sui princess fled in disarray and scattered; the rest of the masses prostrated themselves. When Jing's army arrived, they all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli and the Sui princess fled in disorder while the rest threw themselves down. When Jing's main force arrived, the whole army surrendered.

sentences.zh: 軍還，授左武候中郎將。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Central Commander of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made a commander in the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，轉左衛勳一府中郎將，從左衛大將軍程知節征賀魯，為前軍總管。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was transferred to Central Commander of the First Merit Office of the Left Guard, following Grand General of the Left Guard Cheng Zhijie in the campaign against Helu, as commander of the vanguard army.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui he was transferred to the Left Guard and joined Grand General Cheng Zhijie in the campaign against Helu as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至鷹娑川，突厥有二萬騎來拒，總管蘇海政與戰，互有前卻。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yingsuo River, the Turks had twenty thousand cavalry come to resist; Commander Su Haizheng joined battle with them, each side advancing and retreating.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yingsuo River twenty thousand Turk horsemen blocked their path. Commander Su Haizheng engaged them in a seesaw fight.

sentences.zh: 既而突厥別部鼠尼施等又領二萬餘騎續至。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Turk separate division Shunishi and others again led more than twenty thousand cavalry arriving in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Then another Turk force led by Shunishi arrived with more than twenty thousand additional horsemen.

sentences.zh: 定方正歇馬，隔一小嶺，去知節十許裏，望見塵起，率五百騎馳往擊之，賊眾大潰，追奔二十里，殺千五百餘人，獲馬二千匹，死馬及所棄甲仗，綿亙山野，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Dingfang was just resting his horses, separated by a small ridge, about ten-odd li from Zhijie; he saw dust rise, led five hundred cavalry in gallop to strike them — the rebel masses greatly collapsed. Pursuing in flight twenty li, he killed more than fifteen hundred men, captured two thousand horses; dead horses and abandoned armour and weapons stretched across mountains and fields beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang was resting his horses a ridge away, some ten li from Zhijie, when he saw dust on the horizon. He led five hundred cavalry in a charge that routed the enemy. He pursued twenty li, killed more than fifteen hundred men, and captured two thousand horses; the dead horses and abandoned arms littered the hills beyond count.

sentences.zh: 副大總管王文度害其功，謂知節曰：“雖雲破賊，官軍亦有死傷，蓋決成敗法耳，何為此事？

translations.literal: Deputy supreme commander Wang Wendu envied his achievement and said to Zhijie: "Although it is said the bandits were broken, the official army also has dead and wounded — this is after all the method of deciding victory and defeat. Why do this matter?
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Wang Wendu, jealous of his success, told Zhijie, "Even if the enemy was beaten, our own men were killed and wounded. Battles should decide the outcome, not reckless gambles. Why allow such rashness?

sentences.zh: 自今正可結為方陣，輜重並納腹中，四面布隊，人馬被甲，賊來即戰，自保萬全。

translations.literal: From now on one should rightly form a square formation, baggage and heavy equipment all taken into the belly, troops arrayed on four sides, men and horses armoured — when bandits come then fight, self-preservation ten thousand times secure.
translations.idiomatic: From now on we should march in square formation, keep supplies inside the column, deploy on all sides with men and horses in armour, and fight only when the enemy comes — that way we are perfectly safe.

sentences.zh: 無為輕脫，致有傷損。

translations.literal: Do not act lightly and loosely, causing injury and loss."
translations.idiomatic: Do not take risks that bring casualties."

sentences.zh: ”又矯稱別奉聖旨，以知節恃勇輕敵，使文度為其節製，遂收軍不許深入。

translations.literal: He also falsely claimed to have received a separate imperial edict, on the grounds that Zhijie relied on courage and despised the enemy, and had Wendu restrain him; he then recalled the army and would not permit a deep advance.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged a separate imperial order, alleging that Zhijie was rash and overconfident, and had Wendu placed in command over him; the army was then pulled back and forbidden to press deep into enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 終日跨馬被甲結陣，由是馬多瘦死，士卒疲勞，無有戰誌。

translations.literal: All day long they mounted horses, donned armour, and formed battle lines; because of this many horses wasted away and died, the soldiers grew weary, and there was no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day the men sat mounted in armour in battle formation; horses wasted away and died in large numbers, the troops were exhausted, and fighting spirit vanished.

sentences.zh: 定方謂知節曰：“本來討賊，今乃自守，馬餓兵疲，逢賊即敗。

translations.literal: Dingfang said to Zhijie: "We came originally to attack bandits, yet now we are merely defending ourselves; horses hungry and troops weary — if we meet bandits we will be defeated at once.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang told Zhijie, "We set out to destroy the enemy, and now we are only holding defensive positions. With starving horses and exhausted men, we will be beaten the moment we meet the foe.

sentences.zh: 怯懦如此，何功可立！

translations.literal: Cowardice like this — what achievement can be established!
translations.idiomatic: With such timidity, how can we accomplish anything!

sentences.zh: 又公為大將，閫外之事，不許自專，別遣軍副，專其號令，理必不然。

translations.literal: Moreover, you are the supreme commander; affairs outside the capital gate may not be decided on one's own authority — to send a separate deputy to monopolize the orders, by reason this cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you are the commander-in-chief, with full authority in the field. It makes no sense that a separate deputy would be sent to take sole control of the orders.

sentences.zh: 須囚縶文度，飛表奏之。

translations.literal: We must bind and imprison Wendu and dispatch an urgent memorial reporting this."
translations.idiomatic: Wendu must be arrested and bound, and an urgent report sent to the throne."

sentences.zh: ”知節不從。

translations.literal: Zhijie did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie refused.

sentences.zh: 至恒篤城，有胡降附，文度又曰：“比我兵回，彼還作賊，不如盡殺，取其資財。

translations.literal: When they reached Hengdu City, there were barbarians who surrendered and submitted; Wendu again said: "By the time our army returns, they will again become bandits — better to kill them all and take their goods and wealth."
translations.idiomatic: At Hengdu City some tribesmen surrendered. Wendu again proposed, "Once our army withdraws, they will turn bandit again. We should kill them all and seize their property."

sentences.zh: ”定方曰：“如此，自作賊耳，何成伐叛？

translations.literal: Dingfang said: "Acting thus, we ourselves become bandits — how can this accomplish the suppression of rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang replied, "That would make us the bandits. How would that count as putting down rebellion?"

sentences.zh: ”文度不從。

translations.literal: Wendu did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及分財，唯定方一無所取。

translations.literal: When the spoils were divided, only Dingfang took nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: When the loot was distributed, Dingfang alone took nothing.

sentences.zh: 師還，文度坐處死，後得除名。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Wendu was sentenced to death for his crime; later he was granted removal from the register instead.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, Wendu was condemned to death for his conduct, though the sentence was later commuted to dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢定方為行軍大總管，又征賀魯，以任雅相、回紇婆潤為副。

translations.literal: The next year Dingfang was promoted to Grand General on Campaign and again marched against Helu, with Ren Yaxiang and the Uyghur Boren as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Dingfang was appointed Grand General on Campaign for another expedition against Helu, with Ren Yaxiang and the Uyghur leader Boren as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 自金山之北，指處木昆部落，大破之。

translations.literal: From north of Mount Jin he struck toward the Chumukun tribe and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from north of Mount Jin, he struck the Chumukun tribe and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 其俟斤懶獨祿以眾萬餘帳來降，定方撫之，發其千騎進至突騎施部。

translations.literal: Their yabghu Nandulu came to surrender with more than ten thousand tents of followers; Dingfang comforted them, then sent forth a thousand of their horsemen and advanced to the Turgish division.
translations.idiomatic: The yabghu Nandulu submitted with more than ten thousand tents of his people. Dingfang received them kindly, then took a thousand of their horsemen and pressed on into Turgish territory.

sentences.zh: 賀魯率胡祿屋闕啜、懾舍提暾啜、鼠尼施處半啜、處木昆屈律啜、五努失畢兵馬，眾且十萬，來拒官軍，定方率回紇及漢兵萬餘人擊之。

translations.literal: Helu led the forces of the Holuwi yabghu, Shefat yabghu, Shunishi Chuban yabghu, Chumukun Qulu yabghu, and the On Ok confederation — troops numbering nearly one hundred thousand — to resist the imperial army; Dingfang led more than ten thousand Uyghurs and Han soldiers to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Helu mustered nearly one hundred thousand men from the Holuwi, Shefat, Shunishi Chuban, and Chumukun Qulu yabghus and the On Ok confederation to block the imperial army. Dingfang led a force of more than ten thousand Uyghur and Han troops against them.

sentences.zh: 賊輕定方兵少，四面圍之，定方令步卒據原，攢槊外向，親領漢騎陣於北原。

translations.literal: The rebels despised Dingfang's few troops and surrounded them on four sides; Dingfang ordered the infantry to hold the high ground, massing spears pointing outward, and personally led the Han cavalry in formation on the northern plain.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, thinking Dingfang's force too small, closed in from all sides. Dingfang had his foot soldiers hold the high ground with spears bristling outward, while he personally drew up the Han cavalry on the northern plain.

sentences.zh: 賊先擊步軍，三衝不入，定方乘勢擊之，賊遂大潰，追奔三十里，殺人馬數萬。

translations.literal: The rebels first attacked the infantry; three charges failed to break in. Dingfang seized the momentum and struck them — the rebels then collapsed in great disorder. Pursuing the rout thirty li, he killed men and horses numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels assaulted the infantry first but failed to break through after three charges. Dingfang counterattacked at the right moment and routed them completely. He pursued thirty li, killing tens of thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 明日，整兵復進。

translations.literal: The next day he reformed his troops and advanced again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he regrouped and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 於是胡祿屋等五努失畢悉眾來降，賀魯獨與處木昆屈律啜數百騎西走。

translations.literal: Thereupon Holuwi and the rest of the On Ok submitted with all their forces; Helu alone fled west with Chumukun Qulu yabghu and several hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Holuwi and the other On Ok leaders then surrendered with their full forces. Helu alone fled west with the Chumukun Qulu yabghu and a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 餘五咄六聞賀魯敗，各向南道降於步真，於是西蕃悉定。

translations.literal: The remaining five Dulu tribes, hearing of Helu's defeat, each submitted by the southern route to Buzhen; thus the western barbarians were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining Dulu tribes, learning of Helu's defeat, each submitted to Buzhen by the southern route, and the western frontier was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 唯賀魯及咥運率其牙內餘眾而奔，定方追之，復大戰於伊麗水上，殺獲略盡。

translations.literal: Only Helu and Jieyun led the remaining forces of the royal encampment in flight; Dingfang pursued them and again fought a great battle on the Ili River, killing and capturing nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Only Helu and Jieyun escaped with the remnants of the royal guard. Dingfang pursued them and fought another great battle on the Ili River, killing or capturing nearly the entire force.

sentences.zh: 賀魯及咥運十餘騎逼夜亡走，定方遣副將蕭嗣業追捕之，至於石國，擒之而還。

translations.literal: Helu and Jieyun, with a dozen-odd horsemen, fled under cover of night; Dingfang sent Deputy Commander Xiao Siye in pursuit, reaching as far as the Stone Kingdom, where he captured them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and Jieyun fled by night with barely a dozen horsemen. Dingfang sent Deputy Commander Xiao Siye in pursuit all the way to the Stone Kingdom, where he captured them and brought them back.

sentences.zh: 高宗臨軒，定方戎服操賀魯以獻，列其地為州縣，極於西海。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong received him at the palace steps; Dingfang, in military garb, led Helu forward to present him. The conquered lands were organized into prefectures and counties, extending to the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong received the captives at the palace. Dingfang, still in armor, presented Helu before the throne. The conquered territory was organized into prefectures and counties as far as the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 定方以功遷左驍衛大將軍，封刑國公，又封子慶節為武邑縣公。

translations.literal: For his merit Dingfang was transferred to Grand General of the Left Xiaoqi Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Xing State, and his son Qingjie was also enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements Dingfang was promoted to Grand General of the Left Xiaoqi Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing. His son Qingjie was enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.

sentences.zh: 俄有思結闕俟斤都曼先鎮諸胡，擁其所部及疏勒、朱俱般、蔥嶺三國復叛，詔定方為安撫大使，率兵討之。

translations.literal: Soon the Sijie yabghu Dudman, who had formerly governed the various barbarians, gathered his following together with the three states of Kashgar, Jujpan, and the Onion Range and rebelled again; an edict appointed Dingfang Pacification Commissioner and ordered him to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Sijie yabghu Dudman, who had once governed the western tribes, rallied his own people together with Kashgar, Jujpan, and the Onion Range and rebelled again. Dingfang was appointed Pacification Commissioner and ordered to lead an expedition against them.

sentences.zh: 至葉葉水，而賊保馬頭川，於是選精卒一萬人、馬三千匹馳掩襲之，一日一夜行三百里，詰朝至城西十里。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yeya River, he found the rebels holding Matou River; he then selected ten thousand elite soldiers and three thousand horses for a swift surprise attack — in one day and one night they marched three hundred li, and at dawn reached ten li west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Yeya River, the rebels were entrenched at Matou River. He selected ten thousand elite troops and three thousand horses for a forced march and surprise attack, covering three hundred li in a day and a night and arriving ten li west of the city at dawn.

sentences.zh: 都曼大驚，率兵拒戰於城門之外，賊師敗績，退保馬保城，王師進屯其門。

translations.literal: Dudman was greatly alarmed and led troops to resist battle outside the city gate; the rebel army was defeated, retreated to hold Mabao City, and the imperial army advanced and encamped at its gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dudman was taken completely by surprise and marched out to fight before the city gates. His army was beaten and fell back to Mabao City, where the imperial forces encamped at the gates.

sentences.zh: 入夜，諸軍漸至，四面圍之，伐木為攻具，布列城下。

translations.literal: After nightfall the various armies gradually arrived, surrounded the city on four sides, felled trees to make siege engines, and arrayed them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall the rest of the army had arrived and invested the city on all sides. Trees were cut for siege engines and deployed beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 都曼自知不免，麵縛開門出降。

translations.literal: Dudman, knowing he could not escape, bound his own face and opened the gate to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no way out, Dudman came out with his face bound in surrender.

sentences.zh: 俘還至東都，高宗禦乾陽殿，定方操都曼特勒獻之，蔥嶺以西悉定。

translations.literal: With the captive he returned to the Eastern Capital; Emperor Gaozong attended at Qianyang Hall, and Dingfang led the captive Dudman forward to present him; west of the Onion Range was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang returned with his captive to the Eastern Capital. Emperor Gaozong received him at Qianyang Hall, and Dingfang presented Dudman before the throne. All lands west of the Onion Range were now pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功加食邢州钜鹿真邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted an additional five hundred taxable households in Julu District of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was granted an additional five hundred households in Julu District of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，從幸太原，製授熊津道大總管，率師討百濟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, accompanying the emperor on a visit to Taiyuan, he was appointed by imperial decree Grand General of the Ungjin Route and led an army to attack Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianqing, while accompanying the emperor to Taiyuan, he was appointed Grand General of the Ungjin Route and ordered to lead a campaign against Baekje.

sentences.zh: 定方自城山濟海，至熊津江口，賊屯兵據江。

translations.literal: Dingfang crossed the sea from Mount Cheng and reached the mouth of the Ungjin River, where rebel troops were encamped holding the river.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang put to sea from Mount Cheng and reached the mouth of the Ungjin River, where Baekje forces were encamped along the shore.

sentences.zh: 定方升東岸，乘山而陣，與之大戰，揚帆蓋海，相續而至。

translations.literal: Dingfang ascended the eastern bank, took position on the heights, and joined them in great battle; sails spread and covered the sea as ships arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang landed on the eastern shore, formed his battle line on the heights, and joined battle. Ships with sails spread wide covered the sea as they arrived in continuous waves.

sentences.zh: 賊師敗績，死者數千人，自餘奔散。

translations.literal: The rebel army was defeated; several thousand were killed, and the rest fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Baekje army was routed; several thousand were killed and the rest fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 遇潮且上，連舳入江，定方於岸上擁陣，水陸齊進，飛楫鼓噪，直趣真都。

translations.literal: Meeting the rising tide, they linked ships and entered the river; Dingfang held formation on shore while land and water advanced together, oars flying and drums roaring, pressing straight toward the capital Sabi.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the incoming tide, the fleet linked ships and entered the river. Dingfang held his formation on shore while land and sea forces advanced together, oars flashing and drums thundering, driving straight for the capital at Sabi.

sentences.zh: 去城二十許裏，賊傾國來拒，大戰破之，殺虜萬餘人，追奔入郭。

translations.literal: Some twenty-odd li from the city, the rebels mustered the whole nation to resist; in a great battle he broke them, killing and capturing more than ten thousand men, and pursued the rout into the outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Some twenty li from the city the Baekje army mustered its full strength to resist. Dingfang broke them in a pitched battle, killing or capturing more than ten thousand men, and drove the fleeing enemy through the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 其王義慈及太子隆奔於北境，定方進圍其城。

translations.literal: Their king Uija and Crown Prince Nulji fled to the northern frontier; Dingfang advanced and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: King Uija and Crown Prince Nulji fled to the northern frontier while Dingfang advanced to besiege the capital.

sentences.zh: 義慈次子泰自立為王，嫡孫文思曰：“王與太子雖並出城，而身見在，叔總兵馬，即擅為王，假令漢兵退，我父子當不全矣。

translations.literal: Uija's second son Tai declared himself king; the legitimate grandson Wensii said: "Although the king and crown prince both left the city, they are still alive; my uncle commands the army yet has presumptuously made himself king — if the Han army should withdraw, my father and I will surely not survive intact."
translations.idiomatic: Uija's second son Tai declared himself king. The legitimate heir Wensii said, "The king and crown prince may have left the city, but they are still alive. My uncle has seized command and made himself king. If the Tang army withdraws, my father and I will not survive."

sentences.zh: ”遂率其左右投城而下，百姓從之，泰不能止。

translations.literal: He then led his attendants in throwing themselves down from the wall; the common people followed, and Tai could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his attendants over the wall in surrender, and the townspeople followed. Tai could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 定方命卒登城建幟，於是泰開門頓顙。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered soldiers to ascend the wall and raise banners; thereupon Tai opened the gate and bowed his forehead to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang had his soldiers climb the walls and raise banners. Tai then opened the gates and prostrated himself in surrender.

sentences.zh: 其大將禰植又將義慈來降，太子隆並與諸城主皆同送款。

translations.literal: His general Niceul also brought Uija to surrender; Crown Prince Nulji together with the lords of the various cities all likewise submitted their allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: General Niceul also brought Uija in to surrender. Crown Prince Nulji and the governors of the outlying cities all submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 百濟悉平，分其地為六州。

translations.literal: Baekje was entirely pacified, and its territory was divided into six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje was fully conquered and its territory divided into six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 俘義慈及隆、泰等獻於東都。

translations.literal: The captives Uija, Nulji, Tai, and the others were presented at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The captives Uija, Nulji, Tai, and the others were presented at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 定方前後滅三國，皆生擒其主。

translations.literal: Dingfang, in three successive conquests, each time captured the ruler alive.
translations.idiomatic: In three campaigns Dingfang had destroyed three kingdoms and captured each ruler alive.

sentences.zh: 賞賜珍寶，不可勝計，仍拜其子慶節為尚輦奉禦，定方俄遷左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Rewards of precious treasures were beyond counting; his son Qingjie was also appointed Palanquin Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, and Dingfang was soon transferred to Grand General of the Left Wuwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was showered with treasures beyond count. His son Qingjie was appointed Palanquin Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, and Dingfang was soon promoted to Grand General of the Left Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Qianfeng at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞而傷惜，謂侍臣曰：“蘇定方於國有功，例合褒贈，卿等不言，遂使哀榮未及。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, hearing this, grieved and said to his attending ministers: "Su Dingfang had merit for the state; by precedent he should have received posthumous honors — you did not speak of it, and so mourning and glory did not reach him in time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong heard the news, he was deeply grieved and told his ministers, "Su Dingfang served the state with distinction and should by custom have received posthumous honors. None of you raised it, and so he was denied the recognition he deserved.

sentences.zh: 興言及此，不覺嗟悼。

translations.literal: Speaking of this, I cannot help sighing in mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Even to speak of it fills me with sorrow."

sentences.zh: ”遽下詔贈幽州都督，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He immediately issued an edict posthumously appointing him Governor of You Prefecture, with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately issued an edict posthumously appointing Dingfang Governor of You Prefecture with the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 薛仁貴，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Xue Rengui was a man of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui was a native of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，太宗親征遼東，仁貴謁將軍張士貴應募，請從行。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguan era, when Emperor Taizong personally campaigned against Liaodong, Rengui called on General Zhang Shigui to enlist and requested to accompany the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguan era, when Emperor Taizong personally marched against Liaodong, Rengui sought out General Zhang Shigui to enlist and asked to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至安地，有郎將劉君昂為賊所圍甚急，仁貴往救之，躍馬徑前，手斬賊將，懸其頭於馬鞍，賊皆懾伏，仁貴遂知名。

translations.literal: Reaching Andi, there was a commandant Liu Jun'ang who was surrounded by bandits in extreme urgency; Rengui went to rescue him, leaped his horse straight forward, personally beheaded a rebel commander, hung the head on his saddle, and the bandits all cowered and submitted — Rengui thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: At Andi, Commandant Liu Jun'ang was in dire straits, surrounded by the enemy. Rengui rode to his rescue, charged straight in, beheaded an enemy commander with his own hand, and hung the head from his saddle. The enemy cowered before him, and Rengui's name became known.

sentences.zh: 及大軍攻安地城，高麗莫離支遣將高延壽、高惠真率兵二十五萬來拒戰，依山結營，太宗分命諸將四面擊之。

translations.literal: When the great army attacked Andi City, the Goguryeo regent Yeon Gaesomun sent generals Gao Yanshou and Gao Huizhen leading two hundred fifty thousand troops to resist battle; they encamped relying on the hills, and Taizong divided orders among the generals to attack on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army besieged Andi, the Goguryeo regent Yeon Gaesomun sent Generals Gao Yanshou and Gao Huizhen with two hundred fifty thousand men to meet them. The enemy encamped on the hills, and Taizong ordered his generals to attack from all four sides.

sentences.zh: 仁貴自恃驍勇，欲立奇功，乃異其服色，著白衣，握戟，腰張弓，大呼先入，所向無前，賊盡披靡卻走。

translations.literal: Rengui, trusting in his fierce courage, wished to establish extraordinary merit; he therefore made his dress distinctive, wore white clothing, grasped a halberd, strung a bow at his waist, shouted loudly and entered first — wherever he went none could stand before him, and the bandits all collapsed and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his prowess, Rengui sought a feat that would set him apart. He dressed in white, took up a halberd, strung a bow at his waist, and with a great shout led the charge. Nothing stood in his way, and the enemy broke and fled before him.

sentences.zh: 大軍乘之，賊乃大潰。

translations.literal: The great army pressed the advantage, and the bandits then collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The main army pressed the advantage, and the enemy routed completely.

sentences.zh: 太宗遙望見之，遣馳問先鋒白衣者為誰，特引見，賜馬兩匹、絹四十匹，擢授遊擊將軍、雲泉府果毅，仍令北門長上，並賜生口十人。

translations.literal: Taizong saw this from afar and sent a fast rider to ask who the white-clad vanguard was; he specially summoned him for audience, granted two horses and forty bolts of silk, promoted and appointed him Mobile General and Guoyi of Yunquan Prefecture, and also ordered him as permanent garrison commander at the North Gate, together granting ten captives.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw this from afar and sent a messenger to ask who the white-clad warrior leading the charge was. He summoned Rengui personally, granted him two horses and forty bolts of silk, and appointed him Mobile General and Guoyi of Yunquan Prefecture, with permanent garrison duty at the North Gate, along with ten captives.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，太宗謂曰：“朕舊將並老，不堪受閫外之寄，每欲抽擢驍雄，莫如卿者。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Taizong said to him: "My old generals are all aged and cannot bear the trust of command beyond the capital; I have always wished to select and promote fierce heroes — none compare to you.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Taizong told him, "My veteran generals are growing old and can no longer bear the burden of field command. I have long sought a bold champion to promote, and none compare to you.

sentences.zh: 朕不喜得遼東，喜得卿也。

translations.literal: I do not rejoice at gaining Liaodong — I rejoice at gaining you."
translations.idiomatic: I am not so glad to have Liaodong as I am to have found you."

sentences.zh: ”尋遷右領軍郎將，依舊北門長上。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commandant of the Right Leading Army, continuing as before as permanent garrison commander at the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Commandant of the Right Leading Army while retaining his North Gate garrison post.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，高宗幸萬年宮，甲夜，山水猥至，衝突玄武門，宿衛者散走。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui, Emperor Gaozong visited Wannian Palace; in the first watch of the night, mountain floodwaters suddenly arrived and struck the Xuanwu Gate; the palace guards scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui, Emperor Gaozong was staying at Wannian Palace when, during the first watch of the night, a mountain flood burst through and struck the Xuanwu Gate. The palace guards panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 仁貴曰：“安有天子有急，輒敢懼死？

translations.literal: Rengui said: "How can there be a Son of Heaven in peril, yet one dares fear death?"
translations.idiomatic: Rengui cried, "How can the Son of Heaven be in danger while we stand by fearing for our lives?"

sentences.zh: ”遂登門桄叫呼，以驚宮內。

translations.literal: He then climbed the gate tower and shouted loudly to alarm those within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the gate tower and shouted at the top of his lungs to rouse the palace.

sentences.zh: 高宗遽出乘高，俄而水入寢殿，上使謂仁貴曰：“賴得卿呼，方免淪溺，始知有忠臣也。

translations.literal: Gaozong hurried out and ascended high ground; soon the water entered the sleeping hall. The emperor sent word to Rengui saying: "Thanks to your shouting, I was spared drowning — now I know there are loyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong rushed out to higher ground. Moments later the flood reached the sleeping quarters. The emperor sent word to Rengui: "Your shouting saved me from drowning. Now I know what a loyal minister looks like."

sentences.zh: ”於是賜禦馬一匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted one imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方之討賀魯也，於是仁貴上疏曰：“臣聞兵出無名，事故不成，明其為賊，敵乃可伏。

translations.literal: When Su Dingfang was campaigning against Helu, Rengui submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that when troops go forth without a righteous cause, affairs do not succeed; make clear that they are bandits, and the enemy can then be subdued.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Dingfang's campaign against Helu, Rengui submitted a memorial: "I have heard that an army without a just cause cannot succeed. Make it clear who the enemy is, and they can be brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 今泥熟仗素幹，不伏賀魯，為賊所破，虜其妻子。

translations.literal: Now the Nishu, relying on Sugan, would not submit to Helu; they were broken by the bandits, who captured their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: The Nishu tribe, allied with Sugan, refused to submit to Helu. Helu defeated them and seized their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 漢兵有於賀魯諸部落得泥熟等家口，將充賤者，宜括取送還，仍加賜賚。

translations.literal: Han soldiers have among Helu's various tribes obtained the families of Nishu and others, intending to use them as bondsmen — they should be gathered and sent back, and additionally granted rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Our soldiers have taken Nishu families from among Helu's tribes and plan to keep them as bondsmen. These captives should be found and returned, with gifts added as compensation.

sentences.zh: 即是矜其枉破，使百姓知賀魯是賊，知陛下德澤廣及也。

translations.literal: This would show pity for their wrongful destruction, make the common people know that Helu is the bandit, and know that Your Majesty's virtue and grace extend far and wide."
translations.idiomatic: That would show mercy for their unjust suffering, make the people understand that Helu is the real enemy, and demonstrate the breadth of Your Majesty's benevolence."

sentences.zh: ”高宗然其言，使括泥熟家口送還之，於是泥熟等請隨軍效其死節。

translations.literal: Gaozong approved his words and ordered the Nishu families gathered and sent back; thereupon Nishu and the others requested to follow the army and devote themselves unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong agreed and ordered the Nishu families found and returned. The Nishu then volunteered to follow the army and fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，詔仁貴副程名振於遼東經略，破高麗於貴端城，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, an edict made Rengui deputy to Cheng Mingzhen in Liaodong operations; he broke Goguryeo at Guiduan City and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing, Rengui was ordered to serve under Cheng Mingzhen in Liaodong operations. He defeated Goguryeo at Guiduan City and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，又與梁建方、契何力於遼東共高麗大將溫沙門戰於橫山，仁貴匹馬先入，莫不應弦而倒。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Liang Jianfang and Qie Heli in Liaodong he fought the Goguryeo grand general Wenshamen at Hengshan; Rengui alone on horseback entered first, and none failed to fall at the twang of his bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he fought alongside Liang Jianfang and Qie Heli against the Goguryeo general Wenshamen at Hengshan. Rengui charged in alone on horseback, and every man he shot fell at the twang of his bow.

sentences.zh: 高麗有善射者，於石城下射殺十餘人，仁貴單騎直往衝之，其賊弓矢俱失，手不能舉，便生擒之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo had a skilled archer who below Shicheng shot and killed more than ten men; Rengui alone on horseback charged straight at him — the rebel's bow and arrows both failed, his hands could not be raised, and Rengui captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: A Goguryeo marksman below Shicheng had killed more than ten Tang soldiers. Rengui charged him alone. The man's bow failed, his hands went limp, and Rengui took him alive.

sentences.zh: 俄又與辛文陵破契丹於黑山，擒契丹王阿卜固及諸首領赴東都。

translations.literal: Soon after, together with Xin Wenling he broke the Khitan at Black Mountain, captured the Khitan king Abu Gu and the various chieftains, and brought them to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and Xin Wenling defeated the Khitan at Black Mountain, captured the Khitan king Abu Gu and his chieftains, and brought them to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以功封河東縣男。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County.

sentences.zh: 尋又領兵擊九姓突厥於天山，將行，高宗內出甲，令仁貴試之。

translations.literal: Soon after he again led troops to attack the Nine Surname Turks at Mount Tian; about to depart, Gaozong brought out armor from the inner palace and ordered Rengui to test it.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to lead a campaign against the Nine Surname Turks at Mount Tian. Before he departed, Gaozong brought out a suit of armor from the inner palace and had Rengui try it.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“古之善射，有穿七劄者，卿且射五重。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Among ancient skilled archers there were those who pierced seven layers — you try five layers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Legendary archers could pierce seven layers of armor. Try five."

sentences.zh: ”仁貴射而洞之，高宗大驚，更取堅甲以賜之。

translations.literal: Rengui shot and pierced through them; Gaozong was greatly astonished and took stronger armor to grant him.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui's arrow pierced clean through. Gaozong was astonished and presented him with an even sturdier suit of armor.

sentences.zh: 時九姓有眾十餘萬，令驍健數十人逆來挑戰，仁貴發三矢，射殺三人，自餘一時下馬請降。

translations.literal: At that time the Nine Surname Turks had a force of more than one hundred thousand; they sent several dozen fierce warriors to come forward and challenge battle; Rengui loosed three arrows and shot three men dead — the rest at once dismounted and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Surname Turks mustered more than one hundred thousand men and sent several dozen champions forward to challenge the Tang army. Rengui loosed three arrows and killed three men. The rest dismounted and surrendered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 仁貴恐為後患，並坑殺之。

translations.literal: Rengui feared they would become a later trouble and had them all buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they would cause trouble later, Rengui had them all buried alive.

sentences.zh: 更就磧北安撫餘眾，擒其偽葉護兄弟三人而還。

translations.literal: He then went north of the desert to pacify the remaining masses, captured the three brothers of their false yabghu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed into the northern desert to pacify the remaining tribes, captured the three brothers of the pretender yabghu, and returned.

sentences.zh: 軍中歌曰：“將軍三箭定天山，戰士長歌入漢關。

translations.literal: An army song ran: "The general's three arrows settled Mount Tian; the warriors sang long as they entered the Han passes."
translations.idiomatic: The army sang: "Three arrows from the general settled Mount Tian; the warriors marched home in song through the Han passes."

sentences.zh: ”九姓自此衰弱，不復更為邊患。

translations.literal: From this the Nine Surname Turks weakened and never again became a frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the Nine Surname Turks declined and never again troubled the frontier.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，高麗大將泉男生率眾內附，高宗遣將軍龐同善、高等迎接之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, the Goguryeo grand general Cheon Gwon Yeon led his masses in internal submission; Gaozong sent Generals Pang Tongshan and Gao to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianfeng, the Goguryeo general Cheon Gwon Yeon defected with his forces. Gaozong sent Generals Pang Tongshan and Gao to receive him.

sentences.zh: 男生弟男建率國人逆擊同善等，詔仁貴統兵為後援。

translations.literal: Yeon's younger brother Yeon-geon led the people of the state to strike back against Tongshan and the others; an edict ordered Rengui to command troops as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon's younger brother Yeon-geon rallied the kingdom's forces to attack Pang Tongshan. Rengui was ordered to bring up the rear with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 同善等至新城，夜為賊所襲。

translations.literal: Tongshan and the others reached Xincheng and at night were raided by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan reached Xincheng but was ambushed by the enemy that night.

sentences.zh: 仁貴領驍勇赴救，斬首數百級。

translations.literal: Rengui led fierce warriors to the rescue and took several hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui rushed forward with his best troops and took several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 同善等又進至金山，為賊所敗，高麗乘勝而進。

translations.literal: Tongshan and the others again advanced to Jinshan and were defeated by bandits; Goguryeo pressed the victory and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan pressed on to Jinshan but was defeated, and Goguryeo pressed their advantage.

sentences.zh: 仁貴橫擊之，賊眾大敗，斬首五萬餘級。

translations.literal: Rengui struck them across the line; the rebel masses were greatly defeated, and more than fifty thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui struck them from the flank and routed them completely, taking more than fifty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遂拔其南蘇、木底、蒼岩等三城，始與男生相會。

translations.literal: He then captured their three cities of Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan, and at last joined Yeon.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured the cities of Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan and at last linked up with Yeon.

sentences.zh: 高宗手敕勞之曰：“金山大陣，凶黨實繁。

translations.literal: Gaozong personally wrote an edict of commendation saying: "At the great battle array of Jinshan, the vicious faction was truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong wrote him a personal commendation: "At Jinshan the enemy force was vast and fierce.

sentences.zh: 卿身先士卒，奮不顧命，左衝右擊，所向無前，諸軍賈勇，致斯克捷。

translations.literal: You led from the front among the soldiers, striving without regard for life, striking left and charging right, none could stand before you — the various armies summoned courage and thereby achieved this victory.
translations.idiomatic: You led from the front without regard for your own life, charging left and right with nothing able to stand in your way. The whole army took heart from your example and won this victory.

sentences.zh: 宜善建功業，全此令名也。

translations.literal: You should well build achievement and merit, and preserve this fine reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Continue to build on this achievement and preserve the renown you have earned."

sentences.zh: ”仁貴乘勝領二千人進攻扶餘城，諸將鹹言兵少，仁貴曰：“在主將善用耳，不在多也。

translations.literal: Rengui, riding the victory, led two thousand men to attack Fuyu City; the generals all said the troops were too few. Rengui said: "It lies in the commander-in-chief using them well — not in their being many.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his advantage, Rengui led two thousand men against Fuyu City. The other generals said the force was too small. Rengui replied, "Victory depends on how the commander uses his men, not on their number.

sentences.zh: ”遂先鋒而行，賊眾來拒，逆擊大破之，殺獲萬餘人，遂拔扶餘城。

translations.literal: " He then marched as vanguard; the rebel masses came to resist, he struck back and greatly broke them, killing and capturing more than ten thousand men, and then captured Fuyu City.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the vanguard himself. The enemy came out to meet him, and he counterattacked and routed them, killing or capturing more than ten thousand men and taking Fuyu City.

sentences.zh: 扶餘川四十餘城，乘風震懾，一時送款。

translations.literal: More than forty cities of the Fuyu River valley, catching the wind of awe and fear, at one time submitted their allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty cities in the Fuyu River valley, awed by his momentum, surrendered all at once.

sentences.zh: 仁貴便並海略地，與李勣大會軍於平壤城。

translations.literal: Rengui then followed the coast in seizing territory and joined Li Ji's great army at Pyongyang City.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui then swept along the coast, seizing territory until he joined Li Ji's main army at Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 高麗既降，詔仁貴率兵二萬人與劉仁軌於平壤留守，仍授右威衛大將軍，封平陽郡公，兼檢校安東都護。

translations.literal: Goguryeo having surrendered, an edict ordered Rengui to lead twenty thousand troops together with Liu Rengui to garrison Pyongyang; he was also appointed Grand General of the Right Weiwu Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang Commandery, and concurrently made Acting Protector-General of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: After Goguryeo surrendered, Rengui was ordered to garrison Pyongyang with twenty thousand men alongside Liu Rengui. He was appointed Grand General of the Right Weiwu Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang Commandery, and named Acting Protector-General of Andong.

sentences.zh: 移理新城，撫恤孤老；

translations.literal: He moved to administer Xincheng and comforted the orphaned and aged;
translations.idiomatic: He moved his headquarters to Xincheng and cared for the orphaned and elderly;

sentences.zh: 有幹能者，隨才任使；

translations.literal: Those with ability and talent were assigned according to their capacities.
translations.idiomatic: Capable men were given posts suited to their talents.

sentences.zh: 忠孝節義，鹹加旌表。

translations.literal: Loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and righteousness — all alike were honored with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Acts of loyalty, filial devotion, integrity, and righteousness were all publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 高麗士眾莫不欣然慕化。

translations.literal: The people and masses of Goguryeo none failed to rejoice and admire the transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Goguryeo welcomed the change with evident satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，吐蕃入寇，又以仁貴為邏娑道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, the Tibetans invaded; again Rengui was made Grand Commander of the Luosa Route expeditionary force.
translations.idiomatic: In 670, when Tibet invaded, Rengui was again appointed grand commander of the Luosa Route army.

sentences.zh: 率將軍阿史那道真、郭待封等以擊之。

translations.literal: He led the generals Ashina Daozhen, Guo Daifeng, and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field with Generals Ashina Daozhen, Guo Daifeng, and others to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 待封嚐為鄯城鎮守，恥在仁貴之下，多違節度。

translations.literal: Daifeng had once been defender of Shan City; he was ashamed to be beneath Rengui and frequently disobeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng had previously held Shan City as garrison commander and resented serving under Rengui, so he often defied his orders.

sentences.zh: 軍至大非川，將發赴烏海，仁貴謂待封曰：“烏海險遠，車行艱澀，若引輜重，將失事機，破賊即回，又煩轉運。

translations.literal: The army reached Dafeichuan and was about to set out for Wuhai. Rengui said to Daifeng: "Wuhai is perilous and distant; cart travel is arduous. If we bring baggage trains, we will miss the moment of opportunity. After breaking the bandits we turn back — again the trouble of transport.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Dafeichuan and prepared to march on Wuhai, Rengui told Daifeng: "Wuhai lies far across difficult terrain, and wagons move slowly. If we drag our supply train along, we will lose our chance to strike. Even if we defeat the enemy and turn back, we will still face the burden of resupply."

sentences.zh: 彼多瘴氣，無宜久留。

translations.literal: There the miasma is abundant — it is not suitable to linger long.
translations.idiomatic: The region is thick with miasma; we should not stay there long.

sentences.zh: 大非嶺上足堪置柵，可留二萬人作兩柵，輜重等並留柵內，吾等輕銳倍道，掩其未整，即撲滅之矣。

translations.literal: On Dafei Ridge it fully suffices to set palisades; we can leave twenty thousand men to build two fortified camps, leave baggage and the rest inside the camps, and we with light elite troops double the march — surprise them before they are ready, and at once crush them.
translations.idiomatic: Dafei Ridge is a good place for fortified camps. Leave twenty thousand men to build two stockades and keep the baggage inside. The rest of us will take only light troops and move at forced march. We can strike before the enemy is prepared and destroy them outright."

sentences.zh: ”仁貴遂率先行，至河口遇賊，擊破之，斬獲略盡，收其牛羊萬餘頭，回至烏海城，以待後援。

translations.literal: Rengui then took the lead in marching; reaching the river mouth he encountered bandits, broke them, killed and captured nearly all, gathered more than ten thousand of their cattle and sheep, returned to Wuhai City, and awaited rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui marched ahead with the vanguard. At the river mouth he met the enemy, routed them, and killed or captured nearly the entire force, seizing more than ten thousand head of cattle and sheep. He then withdrew to Wuhai City to wait for the follow-on columns.

sentences.zh: 待封遂不從仁貴之命，領輜重繼進。

translations.literal: Daifeng then did not obey Rengui's order; he led the baggage train and continued forward.
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng ignored Rengui's orders and advanced with the supply train anyway.

sentences.zh: 比至烏海，吐蕃二十餘萬悉眾來救，邀擊，待封敗走趨山，軍糧及輜重並為賊所掠。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Wuhai, over two hundred thousand Tibetans came in full force to rescue; intercepting and attacking, Daifeng was defeated and fled toward the mountains; military grain and baggage were all plundered by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Wuhai, more than two hundred thousand Tibetans had marched to the rescue. They intercepted Daifeng's column, routed his force toward the hills, and seized all the grain and baggage.

sentences.zh: 仁貴遂退軍屯於大非川。

translations.literal: Rengui then withdrew the army and encamped at Dafeichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui pulled his army back and encamped at Dafeichuan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃又益眾四十餘萬來拒戰，官軍大敗，仁貴遂與吐蕃大將論欽陵約和。
