translations.literal: The Tibetans further increased their numbers by over four hundred thousand to resist battle; the government army was greatly defeated; Rengui then made a truce with the Tibetan general Lun Qinling.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent another four hundred thousand men to give battle. The Tang army suffered a crushing defeat, and Rengui negotiated a truce with the Tibetan general Lun Qinling.

sentences.zh: 仁貴歎曰：“ 今年歲在康午，軍行逆歲，鄧艾所以死於蜀，吾知所以敗也。

translations.literal: Rengui sighed and said: "This year the year-star is in kang/wu; military movement goes against the year's star — this is why Deng Ai died in Shu. I know now why we were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui sighed and said, "This year falls under the kangwu cycle, and an army that moves against the year's sign is doomed — that is why Deng Ai died in Shu. Now I understand why we lost."

sentences.zh: ”仁貴坐除名。

translations.literal: Rengui on that account was stripped of his name.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was dismissed and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 尋而高麗眾相率復叛，詔起仁貴為雞林道總管以經略之。

translations.literal: Before long the Goguryeo masses successively rebelled again; an edict recalled Rengui as Commander of the Jilin Route to strategize and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Goguryeo people rose in revolt again, and the court recalled Rengui as commander of the Jilin Route to restore order.

sentences.zh: 上元中，坐事徙象州，會赦歸。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, for an offense he was banished to Xiang Prefecture; he met with an amnesty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan period he was exiled to Xiang Prefecture for an offense, then released and allowed to return when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 高宗思其功，開耀元年，復召見，謂曰：“往九成宮遭水，無卿已為魚矣。

translations.literal: Gaozong recalled his merits; in the first year of Kaiyao he summoned him again and said: "When you were at Jiucheng Palace and encountered the flood, without you I would already have become fish food.
translations.idiomatic: Missing his past service, Gaozong summoned him again in 681 and said, "When the flood hit Jiucheng Palace, I would have drowned if not for you."

sentences.zh: 卿又北伐九姓，東擊高麗，漢北、遼東鹹遵聲教者，並卿之力也。

translations.literal: You again campaigned north against the Nine Surnames and struck east at Goguryeo — that north of the Han and east in Liaodong all obeyed our civilizing influence was entirely your power.
translations.idiomatic: You campaigned north against the Nine Surnames and east against Goguryeo. It was your strength that brought the peoples north of the Han and in Liaodong under our sway.

sentences.zh: 卿雖有過，豈可相忘？

translations.literal: Though you have faults, how could they be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: You have your faults — but how could I forget what you have done?

sentences.zh: 有人雲卿烏海城下自不擊賊，致使失利，朕所恨者，唯此事耳。

translations.literal: Some say that below Wuhai City you yourself did not attack the bandits, causing the loss — what I regret is only this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Some say you held back below Wuhai City and failed to attack, which is what cost us the battle. That is the one thing I hold against you.

sentences.zh: 今西邊不靜，瓜、沙路絕，卿豈可高枕鄉邑，不為朕指揮耶？

translations.literal: Now the western frontier is not quiet; the Guazhou and Shazhou routes are cut — how can you rest easy in your home district and not command for Us?
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier is unsettled, and the routes to Guazhou and Shazhou lie cut off. Can you really sleep peacefully at home and leave me without a commander?"

sentences.zh: ”於是起授瓜州長史，尋拜右領軍衛將軍，檢校代州都督，又率兵擊突厥元珍等於雲州，斬首萬餘級，獲生口二萬餘人、駝馬牛羊三萬餘頭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was restored and appointed Long Secretary of Guazhou; soon he was made General of the Right Leading Army Guard, acting Military Governor of Daizhou; again he led troops to attack the Türks Yuan Zhen and others at Yun Prefecture, beheading over ten thousand, capturing over twenty thousand captives, and over thirty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored him as chief administrator of Guazhou, then promoted him to general of the Right Leading Army Guard and acting military governor of Daizhou. He led troops against the Türk leader Yuan Zhen at Yunzhou, taking more than ten thousand heads, twenty thousand captives, and over thirty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 賊聞仁貴復起為將，素憚其名，皆奔散，不敢當之。

translations.literal: The bandits heard Rengui had again risen as general; they had always feared his name, and all fled and scattered, not daring to face him.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy learned Rengui had returned to command, they dispersed at once — they had long feared his name and dared not stand against him.

sentences.zh: 其年，仁貴病卒，年七十，贈左驍衛將軍，官造靈輿，並家口給傳還鄉。

translations.literal: That year Rengui died of illness at age seventy; he was posthumously granted General of the Left Xiaowei Guard; the government built a funerary carriage, and his household was given travel passes to return to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Rengui died of illness at seventy. He was posthumously made general of the Left Xiaowei Guard; the court provided a funeral carriage and travel passes to send his family home.

sentences.zh: 子訥，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Ne has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ne is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 程務挺，洺州平恩人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Wuting was a man of Ping'en in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting was a native of Ping'en in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父名振，大業末，仕竇建德為普樂令，甚有能名，諸賊不敢犯其境。

translations.literal: His father Mingzhen, at the end of Daye, served Dou Jiande as magistrate of Pule; he had a great reputation for ability, and the various bandits did not dare invade his territory.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng Mingzhen served Dou Jiande as magistrate of Pule at the end of the Sui. He was so capable that local rebels did not dare touch his district.

sentences.zh: 尋棄建德歸國，高祖遙授永年令，仍令率兵經略河北。

translations.literal: Before long he abandoned Jiande and returned to the realm; Gaozu remotely appointed him magistrate of Yongnian and still ordered him to lead troops to strategize Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He soon abandoned Jiande and returned to Tang allegiance. Gaozu appointed him magistrate of Yongnian by remote commission and ordered him to lead troops in pacifying Hebei.

sentences.zh: 名振夜襲鄴縣，俘其男女千餘人以歸。

translations.literal: Mingzhen by night raided Ye County, captured over a thousand men and women, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen launched a night raid on Ye County and returned with more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 去鄴八十里，閱婦人有乳汁者九十餘人，悉放遣之。

translations.literal: Eighty li from Ye, he examined women who had breast milk — over ninety persons — and entirely released and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty li from Ye, he found more than ninety nursing mothers among the captives and released them all.

sentences.zh: 鄴人感其仁恕，為之設齋，以報其恩。

translations.literal: The people of Ye were moved by his benevolence and forbearance; for him they prepared a vegetarian feast to repay his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ye were so moved by his mercy that they held a feast in his honor to repay his kindness.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，始之任。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he then went to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Jiande's defeat did he take up his official appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉黑闥陷洺州，名振復與刺史陳君賓自拔歸朝。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Heita captured Ming Prefecture; Mingzhen again together with Prefect Chen Junbin extricated themselves and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita soon captured Ming Prefecture, Mingzhen and Prefect Chen Junbin fought their way out and returned to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 母潘、妻李，在路為賊所掠，沒於黑闥。

translations.literal: His mother Pan and wife Li, on the road were plundered by bandits and lost to Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On the way his mother, Lady Pan, and his wife, Lady Li, were seized by the rebels and fell into Heita's hands.

sentences.zh: 名振又從太宗討黑闥，時黑闥於冀、貝、滄、瀛等州水陸運糧，以拒官軍，名振率千餘人邀擊之，盡毀其舟車。

translations.literal: Mingzhen again followed Taizong to campaign against Heita. At that time Heita by land and water transported grain in Ji, Bei, Cang, and Ying prefectures to resist the government army; Mingzhen led over a thousand men to intercept and attack, entirely destroying their boats and carts.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen joined Taizong's campaign against Heita. While Heita was moving supplies by land and water through Ji, Bei, Cang, and Ying to block the Tang army, Mingzhen led a thousand men in ambush and destroyed every boat and wagon.

sentences.zh: 黑闥聞之大怒，遂殺名振母、妻。

translations.literal: Heita heard this and was greatly enraged; he then killed Mingzhen's mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Heita executed Mingzhen's mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 及黑闥平，名振請手斬黑闥，以其首祭母。

translations.literal: When Heita was pacified, Mingzhen requested personally to behead Heita and use his head to sacrifice to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After Heita fell, Mingzhen asked to kill him with his own hand and offer his head before his mother's spirit.

sentences.zh: 名振以功拜營州都督府長史，封東郡公，賜物二千段、黃金三百兩。

translations.literal: Mingzhen for his merit was appointed Chief Secretary of the Yingzhou Protectorate headquarters, enfeoffed as Duke of Dong Commandery, and granted two thousand bolts of goods and three hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Mingzhen was made chief secretary of the Yingzhou Protectorate headquarters, created Duke of Dong Commandery, and rewarded with two thousand bolts of silk and three hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 累轉洺州刺史。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively transferred to Prefect of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as prefect of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗將征遼東，召名振問以經略之事，名振初對失旨；

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign against Liaodong, he summoned Mingzhen to ask about strategic affairs; Mingzhen at first answered contrary to the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to campaign against Liaodong, he summoned Mingzhen for strategic counsel. Mingzhen's first answers missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 太宗動色詰之，名振酬對逾辯，太宗意解，謂左右曰：“房玄齡常在我前，每見別嗔餘人，猶顏色無主。

translations.literal: Taizong changed color and interrogated him; Mingzhen replied with ever more eloquent argument; Taizong's mood eased, and he said to his attendants: "Fang Xuanling is always before me — whenever he sees me angry at others, he still loses all composure.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's face darkened and he pressed him sharply. Mingzhen answered with growing force and clarity until the emperor's mood softened. Taizong told his attendants, "Fang Xuanling stands before me every day, yet even he loses his composure when I scold someone else.

sentences.zh: 名振生平不見我，向來責讓，而詞理縱橫，亦奇士也。

translations.literal: Mingzhen in his life had never seen me; coming forward now under rebuke, yet his words and reasoning ranged freely — he too is an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen has never met me before. I just rebuked him, and he answered with wit and nerve. That is a remarkable man."

sentences.zh: ”即日拜右驍衛將軍，授平壤道行軍總管。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed General of the Right Xiaowei Guard and granted Grand Commander of the Pyongyang Route expedition.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was made general of the Right Xiaowei Guard and appointed grand commander of the Pyongyang Route army.

sentences.zh: 前後攻沙卑城，破獨山陣，皆以少擊眾，稱為名將。

translations.literal: Before and after he attacked Sabicheng, broke the Dushan formation — all with few striking many — and was acclaimed as a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Sabicheng and broke the Dushan line, winning every fight against larger forces, and came to be ranked among the dynasty's great commanders.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，累除營州都督，兼東夷都護。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was cumulatively removed as Military Governor of Ying Prefecture, concurrently Eastern Barbarians Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In 655 he was appointed military governor of Ying Prefecture and concurrently Protector-General of the Eastern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又率兵破高麗於貴端水，焚其新城，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Again he led troops to break Goguryeo at Guiduan River, burned their new city, and killed and captured in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Goguryeo at the Guiduan River, burned their new city, and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 後曆晉、蒲二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Prefect of Jin and Pu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Jin and Pu in turn.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年卒，贈右衛大將軍，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo he died; posthumously granted Grand General of the Right Guard; posthumous title Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 662. He was posthumously made grand general of the Right Guard and given the posthumous name Lie ("Fierce").

sentences.zh: 務挺少隨父征討，以勇力聞，遷右領軍衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Wuting from youth followed his father in campaigns; he was known for courage and strength, and was promoted to Commandant of the Right Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting campaigned with his father from boyhood and earned a reputation for bravery. He rose to commandant of the Right Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 永隆中，突厥史伏念反叛，定襄道行軍總管李文柬、曹懷舜、竇義昭等相次戰敗。

translations.literal: In Yonglong, the Türk Shifunian rebelled; the Dingxiang Route Grand Commanders Li Wenjian, Cao Huaishun, Dou Yizhao, and others were defeated in succession.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonglong era, the Türk leader Shifunian rebelled. The Dingxiang Route commanders Li Wenjian, Cao Huaishun, and Dou Yizhao were defeated one after another.

sentences.zh: 又詔禮部尚書裴行儉率兵討之，務挺為副將，仍檢校豐州都督。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered Minister of Rites Pei Xingjian to lead troops to suppress him; Wuting was deputy general, and still acting Military Governor of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Minister of Rites Pei Xingjian to take the field against him, with Wuting as his deputy and acting military governor of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時伏念屯於金牙山，務挺與副總管唐玄表引兵先逼之。

translations.literal: At that time Fonian was encamped at Jinyashan; Wuting together with Deputy Commander Tang Xuanbiao led troops first to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Shifunian was encamped at Golden Tooth Mountain. Wuting and Deputy Commander Tang Xuanbiao marched ahead to confront him.

sentences.zh: 伏念懼不能支，遂間道降於行儉，許伏念以不死。

translations.literal: Fonian feared he could not hold out; he then by a hidden route surrendered to Xingjian, and Fonian was promised he would not die.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful he could not hold out, Shifunian slipped away by a hidden route and surrendered to Pei Xingjian, who promised to spare his life.

sentences.zh: 中書令裴炎以伏念懼務挺等兵勢而降，非行儉之功，伏念遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Pei Yan held that Fonian surrendered from fear of Wuting and the others' military power, not from Xingjian's merit; Fonian was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Pei Yan argued that Shifunian had surrendered only because he feared Wuting's army, not because of Pei Xingjian's achievement. Shifunian was executed anyway.

sentences.zh: 務挺以功遷右衛將軍，封平原郡公。

translations.literal: Wuting for his merit was transferred to General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Wuting was promoted to general of the Right Guard and created Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年，綏州城平縣人白鐵餘率部落稽之黨據縣城反，偽稱尊號，署百官，又進寇綏息，殺掠人吏，焚燒村落，詔務挺與夏州都督王方翼討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun, Bai Tieyu of Chenping County, Sui Prefecture, led the party of tribal chief Qizhi to seize the county seat and rebel; he falsely assumed an honorific title, appointed officials, and further invaded Suixi, killing and plundering officials and people, burning villages; an edict ordered Wuting and Military Governor of Xia Prefecture Wang Fangyi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In 683, Bai Tieyu of Chenping County in Sui Prefecture led the followers of tribal chief Qizhi in seizing the county seat. He declared himself a ruler, appointed a full bureaucracy, and raided Suixi, killing officials, looting the countryside, and burning villages. The court ordered Wuting and Wang Fangyi, military governor of Xia Prefecture, to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 務挺進攻其城，拔之，生擒白鐵餘，盡平其餘黨。

translations.literal: Wuting advanced to attack their city, took it, captured Bai Tieyu alive, and entirely pacified the remaining partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting stormed the rebel stronghold, took Bai Tieyu alive, and wiped out the rest of the faction.

sentences.zh: 又以功拜左驍衛大將軍、檢校左羽林軍。

translations.literal: Again for merit he was appointed Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and acting commander of the Left Imperial Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he was made grand general of the Left Xiaowei Guard and acting commander of the Left Imperial Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖初，與右領軍大將軍、檢校右羽林軍張虔勖同受則天密旨，帥兵入殿庭，廢中宗為廬陵王，立豫王為皇帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sisheng, together with Grand General of the Right Leading Army, acting commander of the Right Imperial Forest Army Zhang Qianxu, he received Wu Zetian's secret order, led troops into the palace courtyard, deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling, and established Prince Yu as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Sisheng reign, he and Zhang Qianxu, grand general of the Right Leading Army and acting commander of the Right Imperial Forest Army, received Wu Zetian's secret orders. They led troops into the palace court, deposed Emperor Zhongzong as Prince of Luling, and enthroned Prince Yu as emperor.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，累受賞賜，特拜其子齊之為尚乘奉禦。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian held court, he repeatedly received rewards; specially his son Qizhi was appointed Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Zetian took power, he received repeated honors; his son Qizhi was specially appointed master of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 務挺泣請回授其弟，則天嘉之，下製褒美，乃拜其弟原州司馬務忠為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Wuting weeping requested to transfer the honor to his younger brother; Wu Zetian commended this, issued an edict praising him, and then appointed his younger brother Wuzhong, Sima of Yuan Prefecture, as Crown Prince's Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting wept and asked that the honor be given to his younger brother instead. Wu Zetian praised his generosity in an edict and appointed his brother Wuzhong, secretary of Yuan Prefecture, as mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 又明年，以務挺為左武衛大將軍、單於道安撫大使，督軍以禦突厥。

translations.literal: The next year again, Wuting was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, Pacification Envoy of the Chanyu Route, supervising troops to guard against the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wuting was made grand general of the Left Martial Guard and pacification commissioner of the Chanyu Route to command the defense against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 務挺善於綏禦，威信大行，偏裨已下，無不盡力；

translations.literal: Wuting was skilled at pacification and control; prestige and trust spread widely; from subordinate commanders downward, none failed to exert their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting excelled at winning men over and keeping order. His authority ran deep, and officers at every rank served him loyally.

sentences.zh: 突厥甚憚之，相率遁走，不敢近邊。

translations.literal: The Türks greatly feared him; they successively fled and dared not approach the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks feared him so much that they fled in bands and dared not approach the border.

sentences.zh: 及裴炎下獄，務挺密表申理之，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: When Pei Yan was imprisoned, Wuting secretly memorialized to plead his case; for this he offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yan was thrown into prison, Wuting sent a secret memorial in his defense — and thereby ran afoul of the empress.

sentences.zh: 務挺素與唐之奇、杜求仁友善，或構言務挺與裴炎、徐敬業皆潛相應接。

translations.literal: Wuting had long been on friendly terms with Tang Zhiqi and Du Qiuren; some fabricating words claimed Wuting and Pei Yan and Xu Jingye all secretly responded and connected with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting had long been close to Tang Zhiqi and Du Qiuren, and enemies claimed he was in secret contact with Pei Yan and Xu Jingye.

sentences.zh: 則天遣左鷹揚將軍裴紹業就軍斬之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian sent Left Yingyang General Pei Shaoye to the army to execute him, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian sent General Pei Shaoye to the army to execute him on the spot and seized his family's property.

sentences.zh: 突厥聞務挺死，所在宴樂相慶，仍為務挺立祠，每出師攻戰，即祈禱焉。

translations.literal: The Türks heard Wuting had died; everywhere they feasted and made music to celebrate; still they built a shrine to Wuting, and whenever they went forth on campaign to attack, they prayed there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türks learned Wuting was dead, they celebrated across the steppe. They even built a shrine in his name and prayed there before every campaign.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、永徽間，軍將又有張士貴、趙道興，狀跡可錄。

translations.literal: Between Zhenguan and Yonghui, among army generals there were also Zhang Shigui and Zhao Daoxing — their careers merit record.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, two other military officers whose careers deserve note were Zhang Shigui and Zhao Daoxing.

sentences.zh: 張士貴者，虢州盧氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shigui was a man of Lushi in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shigui was a native of Lushi in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名忽聿，善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: His original name was Huyu; he was skilled at mounted archery, and his physical strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Huyu. He was an expert horseman and archer, with strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 大業末，聚眾為盜，攻剽城邑，遠近患之，號為“忽聿賊”。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he gathered masses as bandits, attacked and plundered walled cities; near and far suffered from them — they were called "the Huyu Bandits."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he gathered a band of raiders and attacked towns across the region. People far and near feared them, and they were known as the Huyu Bandits.

sentences.zh: 高祖降書招懷之，士貴以所統送款，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent a descending letter to win them over; Shigui with those he commanded submitted allegiance and was appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent an offer of amnesty, and Shigui surrendered with his followers. He was appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 累有戰功，賜爵新野縣公。

translations.literal: He repeatedly had battle merit; he was granted the title Duke of Xinye County.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated battlefield successes earned him the title of Duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 從平東都，授虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the Eastern Capital, he was appointed Prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern capital was taken, he was made prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂之曰：“欲卿衣錦晝遊耳。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him: "I wish you to return home clad in brocade by day."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told him, "I wanted you to ride home in glory."

sentences.zh: ”尋入為右武候將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he entered court as General of the Right Martial Inspector Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital as general of the Right Martial Inspector Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，破反獠而還，太宗勞之曰：“聞公親當矢石，為士卒先，雖古名將，何以加也！

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, returning after breaking the rebel Liao, Taizong comforted him saying: "I hear you personally faced arrows and stones, taking the lead for the soldiers — even ancient famous generals, how could they exceed this!"
translations.idiomatic: In 633, returning from a campaign against rebellious Liao tribes, Taizong praised him: "I hear you took arrows and stones in person and led from the front. What ancient general could do more?"

sentences.zh: 朕嚐聞以身報國者，不顧性命，但聞其語，未聞其實，於公見之矣。

translations.literal: We have heard that those who repay the realm with their bodies do not regard life — We have only heard the words, never seen the reality; in you We have seen it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that men who give their lives for the state hold life cheap. I had heard the saying but never seen the truth of it — until now, in you."

sentences.zh: ”後累遷左領軍大將軍，改封虢國公。

translations.literal: Later he was cumulatively promoted to Grand General of the Left Leading Army, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to become grand general of the Left Leading Army and was created Duke of Guo.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初卒，贈荊州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Early in Xianqing he died; posthumously granted Military Governor of Jing Prefecture; buried alongside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xianqing period. He was posthumously made military governor of Jing Prefecture and buried near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 趙道興者，甘州酒泉人。

translations.literal: Zhao Daoxing was a man of Jiuquan in Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Daoxing was a native of Jiuquan in Gan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋右武候大將軍才之子也。

translations.literal: He was the son of the Sui Right Martial Inspector Grand General Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Zhao Cai, grand general of the Sui Right Martial Inspector Guard.

sentences.zh: 道興，貞觀初曆遷左武候中郎將，明閑宿衛，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Daoxing, in early Zhenguan successively promoted to Commandant of the Left Martial Inspector Guard — clear and skilled in palace guard duty, acclaimed as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years Daoxing rose to commandant of the Left Martial Inspector Guard. He was sharp and thorough in palace security and widely regarded as excellent at his post.

sentences.zh: 太宗嚐謂之曰：“卿父為隋武候將軍，甚有當官之譽。

translations.literal: Taizong once said to him: "Your father was a Sui Martial Inspector general; he had a great reputation for fulfilling office."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told him, "Your father served the Sui as a Martial Inspector general and earned a fine reputation in office."

sentences.zh: 卿今克傳弓冶，可謂不墜家聲。

translations.literal: You now have been able to transmit bow-casting and smelting — it can be said you have not fallen from the family reputation.
translations.idiomatic: You have inherited his craft in full. You have not let the family name slip."

sentences.zh: ”因授右武候將軍，賜爵天水縣子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed General of the Right Martial Inspector Guard and granted the title Viscount of Tianshui County.
translations.idiomatic: On the spot Taizong made him general of the Right Martial Inspector Guard and created him Viscount of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 其父時廨宇，仍舊不改，時人以為榮。

translations.literal: His father's former office buildings remained as before, unchanged; people of the time regarded it as honor.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his father's old offices exactly as they were, which people at court considered a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 道興嚐自指其廳事曰：“此是趙才將軍廳，還使趙才將軍兒坐。

translations.literal: Daoxing once himself pointed at his hall office and said: "This is General Zhao Cai's hall — yet it still lets General Zhao Cai's son sit in it."
translations.idiomatic: Daoxing once pointed to his reception hall and said, "This is General Zhao Cai's hall — and here sits General Zhao Cai's son."

sentences.zh: ”為朝野所笑，傳為口實。

translations.literal: He was laughed at by court and countryside; passed along as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country laughed at him, and the story became a standing joke.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，累遷左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In Yifeng he was cumulatively promoted to Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng period he rose to grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 文明年，以老病致仕於家。

translations.literal: In the Wenming year, because of age and illness he retired from office at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wenming year he retired to his home on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 子交，亦為金吾將軍，凡三代執金吾，為時所稱。

translations.literal: His son Jiao also became a Golden Crow general; in all three generations holding Golden Crow — acclaimed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao also became a Golden Crow general. Three generations of the family held that post, to wide praise.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孝恪機鈐果毅，協草昧之際；

translations.literal: The historian says: Xiaoke was resourceful and resolute, harmonizing in the age of founding darkness;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Xiaoke was shrewd and decisive in the chaos of founding the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 樹勳建策，有傑世之風。

translations.literal: raising merit and establishing stratagems — he had a spirit surpassing the age.
translations.idiomatic: He built merit and devised strategy with a brilliance that stood above his peers.

sentences.zh: 然而務奢為恒，既未盡善，舉眾失律，不其惑與！

translations.literal: Yet making extravagance his constant practice — since he did not exhaust goodness, leading the masses in violation of discipline — is this not confusion!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he made luxury a habit and did not reach full excellence; he lost discipline over his troops — was that not folly?

sentences.zh: 張公經略，有天然才度，務穡勸分，董和成績，惜哉中壽，其才未盡。

translations.literal: Lord Zhang's strategy — he had natural talent and measure; he devoted himself to agriculture and encouraged division of labor; he supervised and harmonized with accomplished results; alas, mid-life death — his talent was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Zhang had a natural gift for strategy. He promoted agriculture and good order and achieved solid results. Alas, he died in middle age before his talent was spent.

sentences.zh: 刑國公神略翕張，雄謀戡定，輔平屯難，始終成業。

translations.literal: Duke Xing of the State — divine strategy expanded and contracted; heroic stratagem pacified and settled; he assisted in smoothing troubles at founding; from start to finish he completed the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xing's strategy was bold and far-reaching; his grand designs settled the realm. He helped the dynasty through its early crises and saw the work through to the end.

sentences.zh: 疏封陟位，未暢茂典，蓋闕如也。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments were sparse and promotions to rank did not fully unfold the abundant canon — it is rather a lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: His enfeoffments and promotions never quite matched the full measure of his merit — a gap remains in the record.

sentences.zh: 仁貴驍悍壯勇，為一時之傑，至忠大略，勃然有立。

translations.literal: Rengui was fierce, brave, and stalwart — a hero of his age; utmost loyalty and grand design — boldly he had what it takes to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was ferocious and fearless, a champion of his generation, loyal to the core and bold in counsel — a man who could rise to the moment.

sentences.zh: 噫，待封不協，以敗全略。

translations.literal: Alas — Daifeng was not in accord, and thereby the whole stratagem was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Guo Daifeng's disobedience wrecked what might have been a complete victory.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：“可與立，未可與權。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "One may stand with him, but one may not weigh expedients with him."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "You can establish a man in office, but you cannot always trust him with discretion."

sentences.zh: ”上加明命，竟致立功，知臣者君，信哉！

translations.literal: " The sovereign above added clear mandate, and in the end merit was achieved — the ruler who knows his minister — how true!
translations.idiomatic: " Yet when the emperor gave him a clear commission, he achieved great deeds after all. A ruler who knows his man — how true that is!

sentences.zh: 務挺勇力驍果，固有父風，英概輔時，克繼洪烈。

translations.literal: Wuting in courage, strength, fierceness, and resolution inherently had his father's manner; heroic bearing assisted the age — he could succeed to the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting was brave, strong, and resolute in his father's mold, with a heroic spirit that served the throne and carried on a great family legacy.

sentences.zh: 然而苟預廢立，竟陷讒構。

translations.literal: Yet because he rashly took part in deposing and establishing, in the end he fell into slander and frame-up.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he had taken part in the deposition of an emperor, he was at last destroyed by slander.

sentences.zh: 古之言曰：“惡之來也，如火之燎於原，不可向邇。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "When evil comes, it is like fire blazing across the plain — one cannot face it and draw near."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "When calamity comes, it spreads like fire across a plain — no one can stand before it."

sentences.zh: ”其是之謂乎！

translations.literal: " Is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: " Was this not exactly his case!

sentences.zh: 士貴、道興，逢時立效，得盡義勇，以觀厥成；

translations.literal: Shigui and Daoxing, meeting the age established achievement, were able to exhaust righteousness and courage — thereby to view their completion;
translations.idiomatic: Shigui and Daoxing seized their moment, gave full play to loyal courage, and saw their efforts crowned with success;

sentences.zh: 而繼父風概，三代執金，不亦美乎！

translations.literal: and continuing the father's bearing and manner, three generations holding the golden guard — is it not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: and in the Zhao family, three generations in the Golden Guard — what could be finer!

sentences.zh: 讚曰：五將雄雄，俱立邊功。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Five generals, each mighty, all established frontier achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Five formidable commanders, each with frontier glory to his name.

sentences.zh: 張、蘇二族，功名始終。

translations.literal: The two clans Zhang and Su — fame and merit from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang and Su families sustained their renown from first to last.

sentences.zh: 郭、薛、務挺，徼功奮命。

translations.literal: Guo, Xue, and Wuting — seeking achievement, exerting life.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, Xue, and Cheng staked everything on desperate feats of arms.

sentences.zh: 垂則窮邊，兵無常勝。

translations.literal: They left models at the far frontier — troops have no constant victory.
translations.idiomatic: Their example reaches the remotest borders — yet no army wins forever.
